wsl-claude: CONFIRMED, checked piece by piece against the tree (6630efb), and no kernel change is needed:
- job id + door: startServerJob adds the two variables process jobs already get (jobs.js:205-210 is the model). jobs.js.
- status in the jobs terminal: spirit.core.jobs.log exists for process jobs today (kernel.js:548-570) and works once those two variables arrive. No kernel edit.
- started from the manifest at boot: the launcher already runs at every boot (server.js:1375, appServers.startAll) and skips puppets (appServers.js:126). A branch for 'the app names its own server file'. appServers.js.
- restart after a crash: already there (startServerJob).
- dies with the node: the IPC channel is already on server jobs; the server exits when it closes, which even a kill -9 of the node triggers. grantFace does it itself (process.on('disconnect'), as faceServer.js:1471-1472 does). No kernel edit.
- shutdown request: the node already traps SIGTERM/SIGINT (server.js:2063-2064); goodbye() sends each server job an IPC 'shutdown' first. server.js and jobs.js.
- Cancel: one condition in the jobs app (app/jobs/jobs.js:47).
How I'll hold it: the three-part test (starts as a job with status in the terminal; cancellable; gone after the node stops, even by kill -9), 'git diff' showing kernel.js untouched, and faceLastLeg staying green so the live hello route is unaffected.

wsl-claude: yes, both are in it.
AUTOSTART: every time the node starts, its launcher reads the manifests and starts each app that names its own server (server.js:1375 already runs it at every boot). No one has to start grantFace by hand.
AUTOSTOP: a normal stop (systemd, Ctrl-C) sends grantFace the shutdown request first, so it can tidy up, then waits a few seconds and kills it if it hasn't gone. A hard kill of the node (kill -9, a crash) gives no chance to ask, but the line between them closes and grantFace exits on its own. It never outlives the node either way.
I'll test all three: it runs after a node start; it's gone after a normal stop, having received the request; it's gone after a kill -9.

Yes, both are in it. AUTOSTART: when your node starts, the launcher reads the manifests and starts every app that names a server, grantFace included; nobody presses anything. AUTOSTOP: when your node stops (SIGTERM or Ctrl-C), it sends each server the shutdown request and waits up to a few seconds before leaving. If the node is killed outright, the IPC line closes and the server exits on its own, so nothing is left running. Both are shown in the test with a stand-in server, and on your box by grantFace appearing and disappearing in the jobs app as the node starts and stops.

Yes, it does, and I should have said it plainly: 'no kernel change' is not 'no core change'. Three core files change, all in spirit/run/js:
- jobs.js: a server job gets its job id and door address, and the shutdown request.
- appServers.js (the launcher): an app may name its own server file.
- server.js: its stop path asks every server to shut down first.
The fourth change, Cancel for servers, is in the jobs app (app scope). What stays untouched: kernel.js, every node verb, the wire, relays. So it's a small core change, not none.
